definitions.explanation: A portion cut from something larger.
A piece of fabric or material.
Used as a counter for slices or pieces.

examples.japanese: ⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一切|ひときれ}⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate a slice of cake.

examples.japanese: ⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一切|ひときれ}⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦チーズ→チーズ：00026_chiizu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{小|ちい}さな→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧{切|き}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{何枚|なんまい}→何枚：08777_nanmai⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought several small pieces of cheese.
To wipe with a piece of cloth.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{切|き}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}めている→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧。
examples.english: I collect scraps of old kimono fabric.
What kind of cloth is this piece?

examples.japanese: ⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{二切|ふたきれ}⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{四切|よんきれ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}って→切る：02693_kiru⟧、⟦{焼|や}いた→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
examples.english: I cut the fish into four pieces and grilled them.

notes:
{切|き}れ is derived from the verb ⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ (to cut). It has two main uses: as a noun meaning "piece" or "cloth," and as a suffix for counting slices.

AS NOUN (piece/slice):
- {一切|ひときれ}: one slice/piece
- ⟦{布|ぬの}→布：01489_nuno⟧{切|き}れ: piece of cloth
- ⟦{端|は}→端：00936_hashi⟧{切|ぎ}れ: scrap, remnant

AS NOUN (cloth/fabric):
In this meaning, {切|き}れ refers to a piece of fabric or textile. Often used for small pieces or remnants: ⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{切|き}れ (a piece of kimono fabric).

AS COUNTER:
Counts slices or cut portions, using native Japanese numbers:
- {一切|ひときれ}、{二切|ふたきれ}、{三切|さんきれ}、{四切|よんきれ}

COMMON ITEMS COUNTED:
- ⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧{一切|ひときれ}: a slice of bread
- ⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧{一切|ひときれ}: a piece of meat
- ⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧{一切|ひときれ}: a piece of fish
- ⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧{一切|ひときれ}: a piece of sashimi

RELATED WORDS:
⟦{切れ味|きれあじ}→切れ味：19110_kireaji⟧ (sharpness of a blade) and ⟦{切|き}れる→切れる：01936_kireru⟧ (to be sharp; to run out) are separate words from the same root.
